# Gaṇakamoggallāna Sutta (MN 107 (PTS MN iii 1))

**ID:** MN 107 (PTS MN iii 1)
**Section:** Majjhimanikāya (mn)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-1
**Title (Pali):** Gaṇakamoggallāna Sutta
**Title (English, from literature):** With Moggallāna the Accountant
**PTS:** MN iii 1

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Gaṇakamoggallāna Sutta* (MN 107; PTS MN iii 1) records a discussion between the Buddha and the brahmin accountant Gaṇaka Moggallāna, who asks whether there is a gradual training (*anupubbasikkhā*), gradual performance (*anupubbakiriyā*), and gradual progression (*anupubbapaṭipadā*) in the Buddha's Dhamma and Vinaya analogous to the stepped instruction found in accounting and other worldly crafts [Kalupahana 1976; Peoples 2013; Dhammissara 2017; SuttaCentral]. In response, the Buddha delineates the sequential path of monastic mental training: beginning with moral discipline (*sīla*), guarding the sense faculties (*indriyasaṃvara*), moderation in food (*bhojane mattaññutā*), devotion to wakefulness (*jāgariyānuyoga*), and the establishment of mindfulness and clear comprehension (*sati-sampajañña*), leading to the abandonment of the five hindrances and absorption in the four *jhāna*s [Sarath-Chandra 2007; Saitanaporn 2009; Anālayo 2019]. The discourse concludes with a simile explaining why only some disciples reach the ultimate goal of Nibbāna even when instructed in this path: the Buddha serves merely as the shower of the path, and it is up to practitioners themselves to walk it [Rogell 2003; SuttaCentral].

Curated parallels include an individual Chinese translation, the *Shujing* (數經, T 70), and a discourse in the Chinese *Madhyama-āgama* (MĀ 144) [SuttaCentral]. Comparative analysis notes that the Sarvāstivāda parallel introduces the four establishments of mindfulness (*satipaṭṭhāna*) into the gradual training sequence directly following clear comprehension [Sujato 2012]. DharmaNexus aligns MN 107 with both T 70 and MĀ 144, as well as several Sanskrit and Tibetan treatises, notably the *Śrāvakabhūmi* of the *Yogācārabhūmi* (along with its Tibetan translation D4036), the Vinaya *Saṅghabhedavastu*, and Śāntideva's *Śikṣāsamuccaya* [DharmaNexus]. Within the Pali canon, the gradual training pericope (§8.2–10.2) is shared with numerous discourses across the *Nikāya*s, including the *Cūḷahatthipadopama Sutta* (MN 27), *Ghoṭamukha Sutta* (MN 94), *Catukkanipāta* (AN 4.198), *Pañcakanipāta* (AN 5.75/76), and the *Jhānavibhaṅga* (Vb 12) [DharmaNexus; SuttaCentral].
